FINAL ANSWER — proportion of Experimental Economics studies conducted in a lab setting: 18/18 = 1.00 = 100%.

HYPOTHESIS (natural language, variable- and relation-explicit)
In the study-level meta-regression file, filtering to the Experimental Economics replication project (project == "ee") yields 18 original studies (18 O/R pairs, one row per id, so per-study and per-pair denominators coincide at 18). Summarizing the setting-modality field online.o ("original experiment conducted online", 1 = yes / 0 = no) over those 18 rows gives 18 rows with online.o == 0 and 0 rows with online.o == 1, i.e. 18/18 = 100% of the Experimental Economics original studies were administered in an in-person lab setting rather than online. Because online.o is constant at 0 across the ee subset, this is a boundary (ceiling) value with no within-project variance. Lab-based administration is therefore effectively universal in this EE replication set: no EE original study used an online sample. Corroborating setting evidence: compensation.o == "cash" for 18/18 (paid in-person sessions), online.r == 0 and same_online == 1 for 18/18 (replications kept the same offline modality), and lab_id (replication-lab identity) is 100% missing for ee. Caveats from the same dataset: only 17/18 (~94%) used student subject pools (subjects.o == "students"; the single exception is ee.4 "Participation", community subjects, which was nevertheless an offline session with online.o == 0), and only 11/18 (~61%) were US-based labs (us_lab.o == 1 — a US-location flag, identical to experiment_country.o == "United States", so it is reported as a labelled sensitivity, not as the setting indicator).

DESCRIPTIVE BLOCK (ee originals)
• project coding: "ee" = Experimental Economics; discipline == "Economics" for all 18; drop == False and aggregated == NaN for all 18 (no drop filter applied, per your ruling).
• n = 18 studies (18 unique ids ee.1–ee.18, 18 unique titles, 0 duplicate rows).
• subjects.o mix: students 17, community 1.
• compensation.o: cash 18/18 — corroborates paid in-person lab sessions.
• experiment_country.o: United States 11, Germany 2, Switzerland 2, United Kingdom 1, Australia 1, Austria 1.
• online.r == 0 for 18/18; same_online == 1 for 18/18.
• NA handling: 0 NA in online.o for ee, so no exclusions; available denominator equals 18.

SENSITIVITY LADDER (numerator/denominator, variable named)
S1 PRIMARY — lab = in-person/non-online, online.o == 0: 18/18 = 100.00%
S2 — in-person AND student pool, online.o == 0 & subjects.o == "students": 17/18 = 94.44%
S3 — student subject pool alone, subjects.o == "students": 17/18 = 94.44%
S4 — us_lab.o == 1 (US-location flag only): 11/18 = 61.11%
The only row moving the student-pool variants from 18/18 to 17/18 is ee.4 "Participation" (subjects.o = community, online.o = 0, us_lab.o = 1, United States) — still an offline/in-person session.

SECOND DATASET (one line, as instructed)
meta-regression_replication_success_data...csv (143 x 15: study, project, ro, rr, fiso, fisr, se_fiso, se_fisr, po, pr, po1, pr1, pm_belief, no, nr) contains no lab/online/subject/country/setting/compensation field; its 18 "Experimental Economics" rows match the same 18 studies, so it was not used.
